title: Bug-Bounty, when present, must be True or False
rationale: Bug-Bounty is not an RFC 9116 field. The IANA "security.txt Fields" registry (https://www.iana.org/assignments/security-txt-fields/security-txt-fields.xml, retrieved 2026-10-29, sha256 cb20345da903627c9761a77f72f19f57f8cd837a9e483381d076a45b7640f120) registered it on 2026-03-07 with this description: "A project or company that may financially reward reporters via a bug bounty program as per section 3.5.5 of [CERT.CVD] can indicate this by adding the line \"Bug-Bounty: True\". Adding the line \"Bug-Bounty: False\" indicates that no financial reward via a bug bounty program can be offered." The registry defines two values and no others. It is a living page, not one of the immutable sources rule.schema.json admits as pinnedAt, so this rule cannot carry a conformance citation; the description is recorded here instead.
policy_note: The match is exact and case-sensitive: the registry spells the two lines 'Bug-Bounty: True' and 'Bug-Bounty: False', and nothing in RFC 9116 or the registry makes a field VALUE case-insensitive (RFC 9116 §2 folds only field NAMES). Every Bug-Bounty value is checked.
applicability: A security.txt body with at least one non-empty Bug-Bounty value. The field is optional.
expectation: Every Bug-Bounty value is exactly True or False.

cases.name: Bug-Bounty: false -- lowercase is not a registered value
no Bug-Bounty field -- the field is optional
